course_name_original: Electrónica para Energías Renovables y Regeneración
course_name_en: Electronics for Renewable Energy and Regeneration

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the main renewable energy sources; the typical loads of electronic renewable energy systems; as well as the optimal way to perform electronic energy conversion between the source and the load.
Understand the principle of electric energy regeneration, the main methods of temporary energy storage, and the main electronic strategies for recovering said energy.
Handle specific laboratory equipment and simulation software for electronic circuits and electronic design.
Design simple electronic systems for energy generation from renewable sources and for electric energy regeneration systems.
Know and apply the regulations that electronic equipment used in renewable energy generation and energy regeneration systems and installations must comply with.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to renewable energies (solar, wind, hydraulic, tidal, geothermal, etc.)
Generators and specific loads in electronic renewable energy conversion systems
Generators (solar panels, wind turbines, etc.)
AC loads (electrical grid, motors, etc.)
DC loads (batteries, electronic loads, supercapacitors, etc.)
Main electronic topologies for renewable energy conversion
DC/DC Conversion
DC/AC Conversion
AC/DC Conversion
Static switches
Electronics for energy regeneration
Presentation of the subject. The work plan to follow. Proposal and assignment of tasks.
Electronic Systems for renewable energies
Electronic Systems for Energy Storage
Electronic Systems for electric vehicles
Electronic Systems for energy monitoring (Internet of Energy)
Electronic Systems for energy transmission
Electronic Systems for Lighting
Group activity TG1 - Presentation and defense of projects completed in ordinary call.
Solar panels. Effect of shadows and hot-spots
Regulation of the Flyback converter for use as equivalent input voltage to a solar panel
Solar MPPT. Perturb, Observe and Wait (PWO) Method
Modeling of a wind/hydro turbine in LTSpice
Modeling of the Permanent Magnet Generator
MPPT for wind turbines
Grid energy injection (grid-tied inverter - GTI)
Energy storage in batteries: DAB converter
Use of the DAB converter or the grid-tied inverter (GTI) to stabilize a DC microgrid (Droop strategies and master-slave strategies)
Simulation of an electronic power system with generation, consumption, and energy storage elements.
assessment_rules: The theoretical exam accounts for 75% of the grade and requires a minimum score of 4 out of 10. The practical exam accounts for 25% of the grade. To pass the practical exam, a minimum score must have been obtained previously in the theoretical exam (minimum 4 out of 10). These rules apply to all calls (ordinary, extraordinary, and differentiated).
